reason: The tether addresses the stated need to keep the experimental tile contained during testing.
expectation: I expect to secure the tether to the stand base; the tile will still need a cradle and power.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the tile in its cradle also seems useful, but I prefer to start with the safety restraint.

effect: The tether is attached to the base; the stand still needs its guide posts and test equipment.
reason: The guide posts should help constrain the tile during the test.
expectation: I expect the posts to attach to the tethered base, making a guided test stand.

alternatives.reason: The tile needs its cradle too, but I want to finish the stand first.

effect: The guided stand is ready for the tile and its power supply.
reaction: The stand is coming together straightforwardly.
reason: Putting the tile in its cradle prepares it for a contained lift test.
expectation: I expect the tile to fit into the cradle, ready to be installed in the stand.

alternatives.reason: The switch and battery also need connecting, but I want to prepare the tile first.

effect: The tile is in its cradle and can now be installed in the guided stand.
reason: Installing the cradled tile completes the physical test setup before connecting power.
expectation: I expect the cradle to fit into the guided stand, with the tether containing its movement.

alternatives.reason: The switch and battery are also needed, but I prefer to place the tile in the stand first.

effect: The cradled tile is installed in the stand; it still needs a power supply.
reason: Connecting the switch and battery is the only offered gameplay action and should prepare the power supply.
expectation: I expect a switched battery pack that can power the tile while the switch is held.

effect: The switched power supply is ready to connect to the tile in its stand.
reaction: The hold-to-lift arrangement fits the need to stop the tile by releasing power.
reason: Connecting the supply is the only offered gameplay action and should let me test the tile.
expectation: I expect the tile to lift in the guided stand while the switch is held, though I don't yet know how much it can lift.

effect: The powered tile rises and settles when released, with the tether limiting its travel; its lifting capacity remains untested.
reaction: The impossible lift is a fun contrast to the carefully restrained test.
reason: The test weight is the only offered gameplay action and should help assess the tile's lifting capacity.
expectation: I expect to see whether the tile can lift the test weight, though I don't know whether it will succeed.

effect: The tile can lift the test weight, though more slowly; the result does not establish its maximum capacity.
reaction: Seeing the load slow the invented lift made the test more interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the weight was most worthwhile: it made the tile's lifting ability something to investigate rather than just an unexplained spectacle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the cradled tile was a predictable fitting without much immediate feedback.

surprise.text: The tile rose without a propeller or balloon, then settled when the switch was released; the tether stopped its ascent.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although several preparations were straightforward and the later choices were compulsory.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the tested tile is used to realize the flying fair, though the setup itself involved few meaningful choices.
